transcript.content: I feel I let a student down today, and I worry this mistake will mean I will never be trusted again. This feeling of failure and of not being trusted began with a specific recent incident at work, and I keep ruminating on it, which affects my work performance and sleep. I feel extremely hopeless, and have even thought about ending my life and leaving this world.
[Counselor] Based on your background and the PMT treatment framework, let us focus on the core issue that troubles you most at present.

growth_experiences: In the past, work-related stress or mistakes often triggered strong feelings of failure and self-doubt, and he tended to cope through repeated rumination, but found it hard to relieve; he had not received psychological counseling before.

exception_events.target_problem: When making mistakes or under pressure at work, the client usually falls into worries about failure and not being trusted, ruminates and seeks reassurance from others, leading to decreased work performance and disturbed sleep.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During a crisis intervention last semester, the client effectively supported a student; the student expressed gratitude and gave positive feedback, and he experienced being trusted and a sense of competence.
exception_events.reason: Clue: On that occasion he was present in time and provided effective support, receiving direct and clear positive feedback, so in that moment the experience of self-efficacy and being trusted was more prominent.

positive_force: Multiple past experiences of successfully helping others and positive feedback
Willing to seek counseling and try reality testing and cognitive balance
Able to recall specific success cases, with reflection and self-awareness
negative_force: Self-blame caused by perfectionism and high self-expectations
Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mind reading
High dependence on external recognition (seeking reassurance)
Rumination worsens anxiety and insomnia, reducing work efficiency
